title: Sprig's Shiny Promise
markdown:
Once there was a young goblin named Sprig who lived in the Starfall Highlands, where rocks twinkled like fallen stars and the air hummed with quiet magic. He had bright curious eyes and pockets that filled themselves with smooth grey pebbles, whisper-soft moss, and anything that gleamed. His very best friend was Pipkin, a tiny mouse whose whiskers twitched at every rustle. Pipkin preferred quiet corners and familiar crumbs. Sprig preferred the next shine.

Every day the sunbeams slanted through the pines, and they played at the edge of the Highlands. Pipkin rode Sprig’s worn tunic pocket, peeking. Sprig pointed at misty peaks and described colours he imagined there. Pipkin nibbled a forgotten crumb. Sprig was kind. He was also forgetful about returning what he borrowed. Once he nearly kept a pretty blue feather; Pipkin squeaked, and the squirrel got it back.

Until one day a sunbeam caught sparkly quartz on a rough rocky ledge, edges like a thousand tiny mirrors. To reach it Sprig needed extra light. He popped over to Elder Grumbleseed’s cozy cave. The old goblin’s beard was winter-frost white, his eye full of secrets. Sprig borrowed a lantern that glowed warm and friendly. “Just till moonrise,” Elder Grumbleseed rumbled, voice like pebbles in a stream. Sprig promised, heart thumping. He zipped up the rocks and filled his pockets with quartz. Then the lantern’s glow reminded him. The elder was waiting. A promise is a root.

Under the gentle shimmer of a sliver moon, like a shy smile in the night sky, they set off. The little silver forest was like stepping into a dream. The leaves were not green but shimmering silver, and when the breeze tickled them they tinkled like tiny bells. Paths wound like sleepy snakes, inviting them deeper. The borrowed lantern cast a warm friendly glow that chased any hint of shadow. Sprig, wonderfully sidetracked, found a patch of mushrooms that pulsed with a soft violet light, tiny shy stars on the forest floor. Pipkin, tucked in the top of Sprig’s cap now, peeked out, nose quivering, trying to decide if those mushrooms looked tasty or a little too purple.

A humming came, happy bees in clover. Around a bend, on a mossy log, sat Willowyn, a witch with a kind face, silver hair in wisps, a basket of lavender, mint, and tiny star-shaped flowers that smelled like sunshine. She was sorting them with gentle fingers. She saw Pipkin’s head. “Is this little one feeling peckish? I have fizzing berry juice for a nervous tummy. It tickles your nose and makes you giggle.”

Juice sounded delightful. Sprig pictured Pipkin giggling. His mouth watered. Then he pictured Elder Grumbleseed’s kind eyes, and moon-high coming whether juice fizzed or not. A promise is a root.

“Thank you, kind Willowyn. Pipkin and I are on a very important journey. We need to return this lantern before moon-high. Perhaps another time.” He patted the cap. Pipkin squeaked, relieved.

Willowyn’s smile did not falter. “Of course. Promises are like the strongest roots of an old oak; they hold everything steady.” The star-flowers glowed a little brighter. “The quickest path is just past the three whispering willows. They will rustle a greeting. May your treasures find their right place.”

With Willowyn’s words making their steps lighter, they hurried on. The three whispering willows did indeed nod their long leafy branches as they passed. Leaves rustled like secrets being shared. Soon the familiar cozy glow of Elder Grumbleseed’s cave appeared ahead, a welcoming beacon. Sprig bounded up, a little out of breath, beaming with pride, and carefully, very carefully, placed the lantern in weathered hands.

The old goblin’s face crinkled into a warm knowing smile. “Ah, Sprig. Back just in time.” The lantern’s glow faded from Sprig’s palms, leaving a faint scent of night-blooming jasmine and a quiet hum of accomplishment. The cave felt warm. The air smelled of comforting earth and dried herbs. Sprig’s heart felt light, like a little bird. Pipkin, no longer nervous about rustles or shadows, scampered from the cap, stretched his tiny paws, and nibbled happily on a bit of quartz Sprig had set nearby.

Ever since then Sprig still loved his shiny treasures, but he returned them promptly, while a promise was still a root and not a story he would have to tell later. Pipkin, who had journeyed through the silver forest and met a kindly witch, found that adventures shared with a thoughtful friend were not quite so scary after all. The quartz stayed in its right place. The lantern stayed in the elder’s. And the Highlands, which had offered every tempting gleam, kept their quiet magic for goblins who could walk past juice with a mouse in their cap.
